info.title: Pigeonpost Nests marketplace core API (proposed)
info.summary: Native Nest jobs, payment authorizations and release review status.
info.description:
**Status: mostly a proposed design contract.** Operations marked `x-pigeonpost-status: implemented`
are served by the postbox under the member API (`/v1`) behind the `marketplace` feature flag,
per account and off by default; none is deployed. The rest are not implemented. A route whose
phase is not enabled answers `404 feature_disabled`. Each implemented operation names its
policy action in `x-pigeonpost-action`; a postbox test keeps the routes and this file in step.

Scope: the four core operations of the marketplace build plan, the seven M0 routes, the M1
reference path (native jobs with zero-priced quotes and payment authorizations, staff review,
attestation and quarantine) and the M2 publisher beta (publisher certification and roles,
templates, source builds, the publisher's review view with redacted findings, listings and
visibility, the catalog, installations with configuration, update, rollback and uninstall,
staff queues and moderation). Operations marked `x-pigeonpost-status: implemented` are served
by the postbox. Paid purchases (M3), hosted test Nests and invite-only or organization
visibility still need their own operations.

M1 moves no money: every quote and payment authorization is zero-priced, and there is no
wallet and no spend mandate (owner decision 2026-11-09, per-purchase payments).

Conventions (same as the Enterprise API, `openapi/pigeonpost-org.v1.yaml`):

* JSON, `application/json; charset=utf-8`, snake_case; timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC.
* Success is `{"data": …}`; lists are `{"data": […], "next_cursor": "…" | null}`.
* Errors are `{"error": {"code", "message", "doc_url"}}` with stable codes.
* `Idempotency-Key` is **required** on the two financial or job-creating `POST`s below. It is
  scoped to the authenticated caller, the acting mailbox and the route, and bound to a hash of
  the canonical request. A replay returns the original response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`;
  the same key with a different request is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Unlike ordinary org API
  replays (24 h), these keys are kept for the lifetime of the job or financial record.
* The acting mailbox is chosen with `x-pigeonpost-identity`, checked against the credential
  exactly as for sending a message.

Authority is decided by `authorize(actor, action, resource)` in the postbox (`policy.rs`), not by
these schemas. A schema validates structure only: it does not establish identity, funding,
review state, revocation or time ordering.

tags.description: Listings run by their publisher: integrations reviewed by staff, jobs delivered to the publisher's service mailbox as `pigeonpost.nest_job.v1` messages, results posted back and delivered to the buyer. Paid with prepaid credits (credits v1): a publisher prices each operation per job in USD; the buyer's credit is held before the job is queued, captured once a succeeded result is delivered (Piyote keeps 10%), and released on every other ending.

post.summary: Submit one job to a Nest operation
post.description:
Admits one durable job under an exact authorization. The server derives the sender, the
resolved target and release, the buyer context, the payer and the trace; the body cannot
supply them. The target is pinned to the quote's release binding: a handle that moved since
the quote never redirects the job.

Free operations still need a zero-priced quote and its payment authorization (which reserves
nothing), so admission, review state and abuse checks always run.

Credentials: a person (member token), the account key, or the acting mailbox's own
capability token. A connector acting for the member gets `credential_not_accepted`.
A plain message or a group message is never turned into a paid job.

Limits: body at most 256 KiB, JSON depth at most 32, duplicate object keys and non-finite
numbers rejected before parsing. `payload` is further validated against the pinned
operation's input schema.

M1: the target is a shared listing address; each paying account gets its own worker (buyer
context) behind it. Only a release with a valid staff attestation over its release digest
and no quarantine or revocation is admitted. `attachments` must be empty and `reply_to`,
when given, must be the acting mailbox.

202.description:
Admission acknowledgement. Retries with the same `Idempotency-Key` and the same request
return this same snapshot, even after the payment authorization has expired; they gain
no new execution authority. Read `GET /v1/nest-jobs/{job}` for current state.

get.description:
The submitting caller, and anyone the job's reply audience explicitly delegates, can read it.
Anyone else gets `404 not_found` (no enumeration). Admission, execution, settlement and
external-effect outcomes are separate fields; a finished execution is not automatically
settled.

M1: the submitting account reads its jobs; the operation's output is inline in `result`.

post.description:
A server-priced quote for one operation of a listing, bound to the caller's account, the
listing, its admitted release and the operation, for five minutes. M1 offers free
operations only: the amount is always 0 and nothing is reserved. The listing must be
published and its release attested and live.

post.summary: Reserve credits for one quoted operation
post.description:
Turns a server-priced quote into an opaque, single-use payment authorization and reserves
the quoted maximum in the buyer's marketplace wallet. The financial authority (the
marketplace module behind the billing bridge) mints the reference, stores only its hash and
binds it to the environment, the caller, the payer wallet, the target release and operation,
the quote and offer versions, the canonical intent digest, the maximum amount, the expiry
and either an exact human approval or a spend mandate.

Without `mandate_id`: a person, signed in recently and strongly when the amount is above the
account's approval threshold (`step_up_required` otherwise). Automation gets
`human_required`. With `mandate_id`: the caller consumes a live mandate that a person created
earlier with step-up; this is the narrow `ConsumeSpendMandate` policy action, not the
`spend` verb, which stays never-auto.

The reference expires after at most five minutes if unused. Once a job consumes it, the
reservation follows the job, not this expiry.

**M1 as implemented:** zero-priced quotes only, so nothing is reserved (`reservation_id` is
null and `amount_minor` is 0) and no money moves. There is no wallet and no mandate
(per-purchase payments, owner decision 2026-11-09): a request with `mandate_id` is refused
with `invalid_request`. The reference is stored as a hash only. A retry with the same
`Idempotency-Key` returns a fresh reference for the same unused authorization (the earlier
one stops working), so a lost response never leaves a usable copy behind.

human.summary: Exact human approval of one quote.

mandate.summary: An agent consuming a mandate a person created earlier.

201.description:
The reference, shown once. It is redacted from logs and telemetry. Possessing it does not
authorize anyone else: job submission rechecks that the caller, intent and environment
match the binding.

get.summary: Read a release candidate's review status
get.description:
A redacted, monotonically versioned projection for the publisher's authorized team: a
personal publisher's own account, or an org publisher's members holding the publisher role
(resolved from live org membership). Others get `404 not_found`.

`allowed_actions` are hints for the console; the server re-authorizes every action. An
approved review is not production admission: security state, revocation, consent, funding
and capacity are checked separately at installation and at every start.
Retrieve a paginated list of all assigned staff roles.

get.summary: Read a release review with its stages
get.description:
The full review of one release for staff: its digests and every recorded stage with its
evidence digest. A person with a live reviewer role and step-up, with no stake in the
publisher; a first-party (platform) release may be reviewed by staff (`first_party: true`).

post.description:
A staff decision on an open review. `release_digest` must be the digest under review. An
approval needs the intake, deterministic scan and behaviour test stages passed and the AI
review recorded (it is advisory and never decides), and also needs `NestAttest`: it writes
the attestation over the release digest and publishes the release's first-party listing.
Only attested releases are admitted to the marketplace pool. A reviewer who owns, filed,
belongs to or built the publisher's release is refused (`staff_conflict`), except that staff
may review a first-party (platform) release, recorded as `first_party: true`.

201.description: The decision, with the attestation when approved.

The build plane picks the request up; when it answers, the review starts with its intake stage and `nest.review.stage_changed` is sent. One build per template version (`409 version_exists`).

Anyone else gets `404 not_found`. Deterministic-scan findings are shown in full (they are about the publisher's own source); behaviour-test findings show only their rule; the AI review is advisory evidence for staff and shows only a count.

post.description: The publisher's admins take an open or blocked review out of the queue (`409 review_closed` once decided).

get.description: The publisher's team: a personal publisher's own account; for an org publisher, the org's owner and full admins and active members holding a live `publisher_admin` or `publisher_finance` role. Anyone else gets `404 not_found`.

post.description: A person acting for a **certified** publisher: the owning account, an org owner or admin, or a `publisher_admin` (`403 publisher_role_required` for `publisher_finance`; `403 publisher_not_certified` / `publisher_revoked` otherwise). The listing serves the release manifest's `listing_address` (`409 listing_address_taken`). Visibility is `public`, `unlisted`, `private`, `invite_only` or `organization`; the last two are reached through grants (`…/grants`, M2b). `price` sets the terms (`currency`, `term`); `amount_minor` must be 0 (`400 price_not_available`).

patch.description: A person acting for a **certified** publisher: the owning account, an org owner or admin, or a `publisher_admin` (`403 publisher_role_required` for `publisher_finance`; `403 publisher_not_certified` / `publisher_revoked` otherwise). Publisher-editable fields only: `title`, `summary`, `description`, `visibility`. Status, release and address change through `publish`/`withdraw`; moderation (`suspended`) is staff's. Sends `nest.listing.updated`.

post.description: A person acting for a **certified** publisher: the owning account, an org owner or admin, or a `publisher_admin` (`403 publisher_role_required` for `publisher_finance`; `403 publisher_not_certified` / `publisher_revoked` otherwise). Needs **step-up**. Publishes the listing on an attested, live release of its template (the current one, or `release_id`), or moves a live listing to a newer one. Existing installations stay on their release until their owner updates. `409 review_required`, `release_revoked`, `security_quarantined`, `listing_suspended`, `listing_address_changed`.

A person acting for a publisher: the owning account, an org owner or admin, or a `publisher_admin` (`403 publisher_role_required` for `publisher_finance`; `403 publisher_not_certified` / `publisher_revoked` otherwise). Its installations stop taking jobs; they can still be read and uninstalled. A suspended listing is staff's (`409 listing_suspended`).

get.description: Anyone, with or without a credential (a presented credential must be valid). Published, **public** listings of certified publishers on live releases only; unlisted listings are reachable by id, never listed. Discovery grants nothing.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Words in the title or summary.

get.description: A person's own installations, active first.

post.description: A person installs a listing they can see (published; public, unlisted, or private to their own publisher team) for their own account, on the listing's current attested release. The installation pins that release: its jobs run it, with this configuration, in the account's own worker. A free listing: `funding` is `test_credits` and no money moves. A priced listing needs `purchase_id`, the caller's paid purchase: after every other check its payment authorization is consumed through the billing bridge for exactly the purchase's intent (single use; the installation takes the purchase's id), and `funding` is `licence`. A replay with the same `purchase_id` answers `200` with that installation and consumes nothing. `400 invalid_configuration` with `details.issues`, `402 payment_required` (with `details.price`) / `payment_pending` / `payment_failed` / `payment_expired` / `payment_revoked`, `409 already_installed`, `intent_mismatch`, `authorization_used`, `review_required`, `release_revoked`, `security_quarantined`, `503 billing_unavailable`.

200.description: A replay of a paid install; the existing installation.

post.description: Called by the billing bridge with the buyer's own token when a checkout starts (`POST /v1/marketplace/checkout` on the bridge). Checks, as an install would, that the listing is published, visible to the caller, from a certified publisher, on an attested release and not already installed, and that it is on sale; then reserves the installation id the payment will admit and returns the exact intent the payment is bound to. One purchase per caller and `intent_id`: a replay answers `200` with the same purchase. An organization buys through someone who is both one of its Nest admins (`ManageAgents`) and a billing manager (`ManageBilling`); the org install consumes the purchase. `403 forbidden` for another account or an org the caller may not buy for, `409 not_on_sale`, `intent_conflict`, `already_installed`.

get.summary: Read a listing's price and offer
get.description: The publisher's team. The price as set, and the offer the financial authority holds for it on the listing's current release line (`on_sale`, `error` when a mirror failed and is being retried).

put.description: A **certified** publisher's admin, with **step-up**. Sets the tax-inclusive price (minor units), currency and term (`one_off` or `monthly`). A publisher-hosted listing is priced per job of each operation instead (`409 per_job_only`; see `/v1/publishers/{publisher}/listings/{listing}/operations/{operation}/price`). The price is mirrored to the financial authority through the billing bridge before it stands: as an immutable offer whose id derives from listing, publisher, release line, term, currency and amount, so any change is a new offer and the previous one is retired. Monthly offers are provisioned there. Publishing on a new major version mirrors a new offer for that release line. Licences already bought keep their terms. `422 price_not_invoiceable` with `details.nearest`, `409 currency_unavailable`, `503 billing_unavailable`.

delete.description: A **certified** publisher's admin, with **step-up**. Removes the price; the listing's offers are retired at the financial authority. Licences already bought keep their terms.

get.description: The installing account, a person. Anyone else gets `404`. Secret values are never returned: `secrets` says which are set.

delete.description: The configuration and its sealed secrets are deleted, open jobs are cancelled, and the worker host deletes the account's worker and its volume (`runtime_removed` says whether it confirmed).

put.description: Validated server-side against the installed release's `config_schema` with the same rules `pigeonpost nest validate` runs. `writeOnly` properties are secrets: sealed at rest, never stored in the plain configuration, never returned. A secret left out keeps its stored value; one sent as `null` is cleared.

post.description: Moves to a newer attested, live release of the same template: the listing's current one, or `release_id`. The configuration must fit the target's schema; send one with the request if it does not (`409 configuration_invalid_for_release`). `409 not_newer`, `up_to_date`, `review_required`, `release_revoked`, `security_quarantined`.

post.summary: Roll back to the previous release
post.description: Back to the release this installation ran before its last update, if that release is still attested and live (`409 no_previous_release`, `release_revoked`, `security_quarantined`). `previous_release_id` is cleared: update again to move forward.

get.description: A person with a live `reviewer` staff role and a recent strong sign-in (`403 staff_required`, `step_up_required`). Each row says whether the reviewer has a stake in it (`conflict`).

post.description: A person with a live `reviewer` staff role and a recent strong sign-in (`403 staff_required`, `step_up_required`). The reviewer must have no stake in the publisher (`403 staff_conflict`). Only an `applied` application is decided (`409 application_decided`). Recorded in `publisher_certifications`, audited, and sent as `nest.publisher.decision`.

A person with a live `reviewer` staff role and a recent strong sign-in (`403 staff_required`, `step_up_required`). The reviewer must have no stake in the publisher (`403 staff_conflict`). Its listings are suspended (so their installations stop taking jobs), queued builds are cancelled and open reviews can no longer be decided. Releases keep their own security state.

get.description: A person with a live `reviewer` staff role and a recent strong sign-in (`403 staff_required`, `step_up_required`). Each row says whether it is first party and whether the reviewer has a stake in it.

post.description: A person with a live `reviewer` staff role and a recent strong sign-in (`403 staff_required`, `step_up_required`). The reviewer must have no stake in the publisher (`403 staff_conflict`). A suspended listing takes no jobs and its publisher cannot change its status. Reinstating returns it to `published` only if its release is still attested and live, its publisher certified and it was published before; otherwise to `draft`.

get.description: The publisher's team. Revoked and declined grants stay as the record.

post.summary: Invite an address, or grant an organization
post.description: A certified publisher's admins. `kind: invite` (an `address`: a mailbox address or handle) serves `invite_only` listings; `kind: organization` (an `org_id`) serves `organization` listings (`409 grant_kind_mismatch`). `discover`, `install` and `invoke` default to true; at least one must be. The answer is the same whether the address exists; its holder hears `nest.invite.received` on `/v1/events`. `409 grant_exists` for a live duplicate.

201.description: The grant (`pending` for an invite, `active` for an organization).

delete.description: The publisher's admins. Discovery, new installs and every later job through it stop at once (`403 grant_required`); installations stay readable and can be uninstalled.

get.description: A person: pending and active invites to any mailbox address or handle they hold, with the listing's title, summary and publisher name.

post.description: The person holding the invited address (anyone else gets 404). Accepting binds the invite to their account; `409 grant_not_live` once it was revoked or declined.
The person holding the invited address (anyone else gets 404). Accepting binds the invite to their account; `409 grant_not_live` once it was revoked or declined.

get.description: An active member: every installation for the org's Nest admins (owner, admin, agent_admin), those they operate for everyone else. Each carries `role` (`admin` or `operator`).

post.summary: Install a listing for an organization
post.description: A Nest admin (`ManageAgents`). The installation takes one of the org's agent addresses (`handle`, in the org's namespace; `409 agent_limit`), and `operators` (member ids) get a live `operate_nest` delegation on it. Visibility: public and unlisted listings; private ones of a publisher the admin acts for; `organization` listings with an organization grant to this org that allows install (`403 grant_required` when it only allows discovery). Members invoke it by sending `x-pigeonpost-installation` with a quote and a job; its jobs run in one worker per listing and org. Removing a member, revoking the delegation or deleting the agent ends that person's use at once; uninstalling deletes the agent address and every delegation on it. A priced listing needs the org's paid purchase (`purchase_id`, from `POST /v1/marketplace/purchases` with `owner_kind: org`; `402 payment_required` without one); it is consumed for exactly that intent and a replay answers `200` with the installation.

purchase_id.description: A priced listing: the org's paid purchase (its reserved installation id).

200.description: A replay of an install under the same purchase.

put.description: A Nest admin. A live `operate_nest` delegation on the installation's agent address; a new one replaces the old.

delete.description: A Nest admin. Their use ends at once.

get.description: The team. Never a private key.

post.description: A certified publisher's admins. `kind: https` (a public `https://host/path`, no credentials) or `kind: deploy_key` (`ssh://git@host/owner/repo` or `git@host:owner/repo`): Pigeonpost generates an Ed25519 key, seals the private half with the vault and answers with the public half to add to the repository read-only. Every host must be on the postbox's allowlist (`403 git_host_not_allowed`). A build names it with `source.source_id`.

get.description: The team.

delete.description: The admins. The sealed key is wiped; queued builds that named it fail with `source_deleted`.

get.description: The team. Staging postbox only: `404 staging_only` elsewhere; `503 test_pool_unavailable` without a test pool.

post.description: A certified publisher's admins, from a `release_id` or a `build_id` of theirs that passed intake and failed no stage (approval not needed; `409 intake_required`, `release_not_testable`, `build_not_built`). It lives `days` (default and maximum: the postbox's `POSTBOX_MARKETPLACE_TEST_NEST_DAYS`, 7 unless set), runs in the test pool only and admits only a test statement (`pigeonpost.nest.release.test.v1`), which a production pool refuses. At most 5 live per publisher (`409 too_many_test_nests`). A day before expiry the team gets `nest.test.expiring`; at expiry `nest.test.expired`, and its worker and volume are removed. Staging postbox only: `404 staging_only` elsewhere; `503 test_pool_unavailable` without a test pool.

get.description: The team. Staging postbox only: `404 staging_only` elsewhere; `503 test_pool_unavailable` without a test pool.

delete.description: The admins. Open jobs stop; the worker and its volume are removed (`runtime_removed`). Staging postbox only: `404 staging_only` elsewhere; `503 test_pool_unavailable` without a test pool.

post.description: The admins. Open jobs stop, the worker and its data are removed, and the next job starts on a fresh one (`generation` + 1). The expiry does not move. Staging postbox only: `404 staging_only` elsewhere; `503 test_pool_unavailable` without a test pool.

get.description: The team. Staging postbox only: `404 staging_only` elsewhere; `503 test_pool_unavailable` without a test pool.

post.description: The admins. The operation's input schema is enforced; no quote, no payment, no buyer. At most 500 a day per test Nest (`429 rate_limited`); `409 test_nest_ended` after expiry or deletion. Staging postbox only: `404 staging_only` elsewhere; `503 test_pool_unavailable` without a test pool.

get.description: The team. Retries a queued job's hand-over and collects a running one's result. Staging postbox only: `404 staging_only` elsewhere; `503 test_pool_unavailable` without a test pool.

The team: created, job, reset, expiring, expired and deleted entries, with ids, states and error codes only. Staging postbox only: `404 staging_only` elsewhere; `503 test_pool_unavailable` without a test pool.
The team. Counts only (active, active by accounts and by orgs, total, uninstalled); never who installed.

post.description: A person who can see the listing. `reason` is one of malicious, misleading, broken, privacy, illegal, spam, other; `detail` at most 500 characters. One open report per person and listing (`409 already_reported`); 10 a day (`429 rate_limited`).

get.description: A reviewer with step-up. `status=open` (default) or `closed`, oldest first, paged with `cursor`. Reporters are not named.

post.description: A reviewer with step-up, with a `resolution`. Moderation itself is `POST /v1/staff/listings/{listing}/moderation`.

get.description: A reviewer with step-up. Filter by `status` and `publisher`; newest first; paged with `cursor`; each with its open report count.

post.summary: Submit a publisher-hosted integration for review
post.description: A certified publisher's admins. A new version of one of the publisher's templates that names a service mailbox (a `/k/` address or handle of a mailbox owned by the publisher's account, or by its organization's internal account; never under `/pigeonpost/`) and its operations. The integration is stored as an immutable release (`build_isolation = publisher_hosted`) with an open review of kind `integration`; staff decide it with `POST /v1/staff/reviews/{review}/decisions` (step-up), naming `release_digest`. No build and no attestation. `422 service_address_not_owned`, `409 version_exists`, `400 invalid_integration`.

201.description: The integration release and its review.

422.description: The service address is not a mailbox of this publisher (`service_address_not_owned`).

get.description: Newest first, at most 100.

post.summary: Run an operation of a publisher-hosted listing
post.description: The listing must be published, publisher-hosted and visible to the caller (an invite or organization grant needs its invoke switch); the input must match the operation's fields. The job is delivered to the publisher's service at once as a `pigeonpost.nest_job.v1` message from the platform marketplace mailbox; the buyer is never named to the publisher. The result is sent to `deliver_to` (one of the caller's mailboxes; default their first). At most 10 open jobs per account (`429 rate_limited`). **Credits**: an operation with a per-job price holds that price on the caller's credit before the job is queued (idempotency key: the job id; a paid job's deadline is at most 7 days so the hold outlives it). Too little credit is `402 insufficient_credit` with `details.available_cents`, `details.required_cents` and `details.buy_url`, and nothing is queued. The hold is captured once a succeeded result is delivered and released when the job fails, expires, loses its service mailbox or is cancelled; `charge` on the job says where it stands. A free operation skips billing. `409 no_mailbox`, `409 service_address_not_owned`, `409 not_on_sale` (a leftover card price and no per-job price), `503 not_on_sale` (the price is being mirrored), `503 billing_unavailable`.

402.description: Too little credit for this job (`insufficient_credit`): `details.available_cents`, `details.required_cents` (USD cents) and `details.buy_url`, where credits are bought. Nothing was queued or held.

post.summary: Cancel a hosted job before its result arrives
post.description: The account that ran it, a person; anyone else gets `404`. A queued or running job becomes `cancelled` and its credit hold is released; a result the service posts afterwards is refused (`409 job_closed`). A finished job is `409 job_closed`.

get.summary: Read an operation's per-job price and offer
get.description: The publisher's team. The price per job (USD cents) and the `per_job` offer the financial authority holds for it on the listing's current release line.

put.summary: Price one job of a publisher-hosted operation
put.description: A **certified** publisher's admin, with **step-up**. What one job of this operation costs buyers, in USD cents (1 to 1000000), paid from their prepaid credit; Piyote keeps 10% of each job and the rest is payable to the publisher. The listing must be publisher-hosted (`409 not_publisher_hosted`) and its integration must declare the operation (`404 unknown_operation`). Mirrored to the financial authority as an immutable `per_job` USD offer before it stands (any change is a new offer; the previous one is retired). Jobs already running keep the hold they were admitted with. `503 billing_unavailable`.

delete.description: A **certified** publisher's admin, with **step-up**. Removes the per-job price; its offer is retired at the financial authority. Running jobs keep their holds.

get.description: The account that ran it; anyone else gets `404`.

get.summary: Download a hosted job's result file
get.description: The account that ran the job. Served as an attachment with `x-content-type-options nosniff`.

post.summary: A publisher's service reports a hosted job's result
post.description: Authenticated as the listing's service mailbox: its capability token, or an account credential that acts as that mailbox (`x-pigeonpost-identity`). Anyone else gets `404`, as for a job that does not exist. `succeeded` needs at least one file; each file is `application/pdf` (else `415 unsupported_media_type`), at most 20 MB decoded (`413 file_too_large`), and must parse as a PDF (`422 file_unreadable`); at most 5 files, summary at most 4000 characters. Idempotent: the same result again answers `200` with `replay: true`; a different one is `409 result_recorded`; a job that expired is `409 job_closed`. The result is then sent to the buyer's mailbox from the marketplace mailbox with the files attached, and kept on the job.

200.description: The job with its result; `replay` says whether this repeated a stored result.

415.description: Not a supported result media type (`unsupported_media_type`).

422.description: The file is not what it claims to be (`file_unreadable`).

get.description: A reviewer with step-up. Ids, states, delivery and error codes, newest first, at most 100; never the input or the result.

memberToken.description: Keycloak member access token for a signed-in person. Human-only and step-up gates use its validated `auth_time` and `acr`.

apiKey.description: Account API key. Automation, even when the account's owner holds it.

capToken.description: Capability token bound to exactly one mailbox (for example a Nest's own agent mailbox). Automation.

ActingIdentity.name: x-pigeonpost-identity
ActingIdentity.description: The acting mailbox (address or handle). Must be a mailbox the credential may act as; a capability token always acts as its own mailbox. Not proof of identity by itself.

RequiredIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
RequiredIdempotencyKey.description: 16-128 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`. Bound to the caller, the acting mailbox, the route and the canonical request hash for the lifetime of the job or financial record.

Operation.name: operation
Operation.description: An operation name the listing's integration declares (lower-case dotted words, for example `hr.research`).

Publisher.name: publisher
Publisher.description: Publisher id (a personal account's or an organization's publisher profile).

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when this is the recorded response to an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

CacheControlNoStore.description: `no-store`: the body carries a one-time reference.

Forbidden.description: The credential kind or the caller's authority does not allow this (`credential_not_accepted`, `human_required`, `step_up_required`, `step_up_unavailable`, `forbidden`, `staff_required`, `staff_conflict`, `not_admitted`, `mandate_revoked`, `mandate_limit`, `publisher_role_required`, `publisher_not_certified`, `publisher_revoked`).

NotFound.description: Unknown, or not visible to this caller (`not_found`), the feature is off (`feature_disabled`), or a named account does not exist (`account_not_found`).

Conflict.description: State or binding conflict (`role_already_held`, `application_exists`, `idempotency_conflict`, `quote_expired`, `authorization_expired`, `authorization_reused`, `authorization_intent_mismatch`, `environment_mismatch`, `currency_mismatch`, `review_required`, `release_revoked`, `security_quarantined`, `access_expired`, `recovery_window_closed`, `review_closed`, `stages_incomplete`, `release_digest_mismatch`, `invalid_request` for a security action that does not apply, `template_exists`, `version_exists`, `listing_address_taken`, `listing_address_changed`, `listing_suspended`, `listing_not_suspended`, `configuration_invalid_for_release`, `already_installed`, `installation_removed`, `installation_changed`, `installation_required`, `not_newer`, `up_to_date`, `no_previous_release`, `application_decided`, `not_on_sale`, `intent_conflict`, `intent_mismatch`, `authorization_used`, `owner_not_supported`, `currency_unavailable`).

PaymentRequired.description: A priced listing without a paid purchase (`payment_required`, with `details.price`), a payment not confirmed or not usable (`payment_pending`, `payment_failed`, `payment_expired`, `payment_revoked`), or a paid installation whose licence gives no access now (`licence_inactive`).

PriceNotInvoiceable.description: The financial authority cannot invoice this tax-inclusive price exactly (`price_not_invoiceable`); `details.nearest` lists the nearest prices it can. Nothing changed.

BillingUnavailable.description: The billing bridge or the financial authority is not answering, or payments are not configured (`billing_unavailable`). Nothing changed.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Body over 256 KiB or deeper than 32 levels (`payload_too_large`).

InsufficientCredits.description: The wallet's available credits cannot cover the quoted maximum (`insufficient_credits`). Nothing was reserved and no card is charged.

FinanceUnavailable.description: The financial authority cannot confirm funding or revocation state (`financial_authority_unavailable`). New work is denied; nothing was reserved twice.

version.description: Semver; a new service address or operation is a new version.

service_address.description: A mailbox of the publisher's account or organization, for example `/acme/hr`.

prices.description: The per-job prices the template's listings carry (credits v1), for the reviewer to see what buyers will pay.

input.description: The operation's fields, strings only; at most 64 KiB as JSON.

deliver_to.description: One of the caller's mailboxes; default the account's first.

charge.description: Credits: what this job holds or cost. `null` for a free operation. `held`: reserved on the buyer's credit; `charged`: captured after the result was delivered; `released`: returned to the buyer's credit.

amount_cents.description: Price of one job in US cents (credits are kept and spent in USD).

content_b64.description: Standard base64 (RFC 4648 section 4); at most 20 MB decoded.

charge_state.description: Credits: the job's charge in the outbox (`null`: free). `refused` means saas_be refused a capture or release for good; `charge_error` says why.

ListingPriceTerms.description: Price terms a publisher sets (M2b). `amount_minor` must be 0 until payments land (`400 price_not_available`).

hosting.description: `publisher`: the publisher runs this service. Pigeonpost reviewed the publisher and the integration, not the code; a buyer's inputs are sent to the publisher. Such a listing is never installed: its operations are run as hosted jobs.

service_address.description: A publisher-hosted listing's service mailbox, as its integration names it.

ListingPrice.description: A listing's price. Free: `amount_minor` 0 and `funding: test_credits`, with the listing's preferred `currency` and `term` (M2b). Priced (payments): the publisher's tax-inclusive price in minor units, `funding: card`, and `on_sale` once the financial authority holds the offer.

listing.description: On `GET /v1/marketplace/invites`: title, summary, status, publisher name.

deploy_key.description: The public key to add read-only, its SHA-256 fingerprint and `access: read_only`. Never the private key.

Error.description: Every refusal. `code` is stable; private resources are never distinguished from missing ones.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable code. Branch on this.

message.description: Human-readable text. May change; do not parse it.

doc_url.description: Link to the error reference entry for `code`.

details.description: Extra machine-readable facts some errors carry.

NestJobRequest.title: Pigeonpost Nest job request v1
NestJobRequest.description:
The client part of a job. The server adds the authenticated sender, the resolved and pinned
target, the buyer context, the payer, the job id and the server trace after authorization.
Fields that would claim those (`from`, `payer`, `amount_minor`, `customer_id`, `approval`,
`tenant`, `model_budget`) are rejected as unknown properties.

to.description: The Nest's address or readable handle. Resolved and pinned to the quote's release binding.

operation.description: The Nest operation, as published in its reviewed release.

payment_authorization.description: Opaque single-use reference from `POST /v1/nest-payment-authorizations`. Not a bearer token for anyone else.

payload.description: Validated additionally against the pinned operation's input schema and the global size and depth limits.

attachments.description: Attachment ids already uploaded by the acting mailbox. Their content digests become part of the intent.

reply_to.description: One of the caller's own mailboxes to receive results. Defaults to the acting mailbox.

deadline_at.description: Must be in the future and no later than the quote, the mandate and any paid access term allow.

client_trace_id.description: Observability only. Never part of the commercial intent, never authority.

to.description: The resolved Nest address at admission (not the handle as typed).

effects_outcome_unknown.description: Number of external effects whose outcome could not be established. They are reconciled, never blindly retried.

result_attachments.description: Result artifacts readable by this caller.

result.description: M1. The operation's output, inline, once execution succeeded; null before.

NestPaymentAuthorizationRequest.title: Pigeonpost Nest payment authorization request v1
NestPaymentAuthorizationRequest.description:
The server derives the caller, the wallet, the amount, the currency, the intent and the
approval provenance from the quote and the credential. Without `mandate_id` the request is
an exact human approval, except an independently authorized zero-price operation.

amount_minor.description: Reserved maximum in minor units of the marketplace currency. One credit is one minor unit.

currency.description: The single configured marketplace currency. Any other value is refused.

NestReviewStatus.title: Pigeonpost Nest release review status v1
NestReviewStatus.description: Publisher-visible, redacted projection. Approval here is distinct from current security state, revocation and installation admission.

kind.description: `integration`: a publisher-hosted integration, reviewed by staff alone (one `human_review` stage, no attestation).

previous_review_id.description: Set on a resubmission; the earlier review stays immutable.

artifact_digest.description: Digest of the Pigeonpost-built artifact under review.

status.description: `changes_requested` also covers a review an analysis stage blocked (its `decision_ref` is that stage's record); `withdrawn` is the publisher's own.

approval_ref.description: Reference to the staff decision. Present only on an approved review; never set by automation.

owner_kind.description: `platform` is Pigeonpost's own first-party publisher (M1), made by the build plane; an application is always `account` or `org`.

amount_minor.description: Zero in M1; no money moves.

decision.description: Automated stages pass or fail; the AI review is always `advisory`; only the human review decides.

reviewer.description: A staff account id, or `system:build-plane` / `system:analysis` for automation.

kind.description: `integration`: a publisher-hosted integration, reviewed by staff alone (one `human_review` stage, no attestation).

integration.description: For an integration review, its descriptor and whether the service mailbox is still the publisher's; otherwise null.

release_digest.description: The digest the reviewer is deciding on; it must be the one under review.

kind.description: `integration`: a publisher-hosted integration, reviewed by staff alone (one `human_review` stage, no attestation).

runtime_updated.description: The worker host confirmed that the release's workers stopped (or that the quarantine was lifted).

Listing.description: A listing. The public read adds `publisher`, `operations`, `config_schema` and `price`; the publisher's own reads add `template_id`, `moderation_reason` and timestamps. The catalog leaves out `moderation_reason`.

status.description: `suspended` is staff's (moderation, revocation); a publisher cannot leave it.

address.description: The shared Nest address jobs are sent to.

operations.description: The release manifest's operations and their input fields. On a publisher-hosted listing each also has `price`: `null` (free) or `{amount_cents, currency: USD, term: per_job, funding: credits, on_sale}`.

decision_reason.description: Staff's reason for the latest decision or revocation.

conflict.description: The reviewer has a stake in this publisher (staff queue).

PublisherRoleGrant.description: The member by `account_id`, or (M2b) by `member_id`, the org member id the org's member list shows. Exactly one of the two.

slug.description: The manifest `name` of every release of this template.

repository.description: Read-only fetch; no credentials in the URL.

release_id.description: An attested release of the listing's template; default the listing's current one.

NestConfigSchema.description: A release's installation configuration schema: the Pigeonpost subset of JSON Schema 2020-12 (`pigeonpost_core::nest_package`). One flat object (`additionalProperties: false`) of `string` (with `maxLength` <= 4096 or `enum`; optional `minLength`), `integer` and `number` (optional `minimum`, `maximum`) and `boolean` properties, each with optional `title`, `description` and `default`; at most 32. `writeOnly: true` marks a secret string (no `default`, no `enum`). Every other keyword is refused by name. Fixtures: `examples/nest-config-fixtures.json`.

purchase_id.description: A priced listing only. The caller's paid purchase (`POST /v1/marketplace/purchases`, paid through the billing bridge); the installation takes its id.

InstallationLicence.description: The licence a paid installation runs under, as the financial authority last reported it. Without `access` the installation takes no jobs and its worker is stopped (data kept); past `deletion_due_at` it is uninstalled and its worker and data removed.

intent.description: What the payment admits, exactly as the financial authority binds it.

release_id.description: Update only: the target release; default the listing's current one.

configuration.description: A configuration for the target release, when the current one does not fit its schema.

funding.description: `test_credits` for a free listing; `licence` for a paid one, whose `licence` says what was bought.

kind.description: `integration`: a publisher-hosted integration, reviewed by staff alone (one `human_review` stage, no attestation).
